title: Automated Inventory Reconciliation for Boutique Retail
business: Boutique retail managers who maintain product catalogs across disparate digital platforms.
problem: Manual reconciliation between warehouse data stores and storefront inventory often leads to overselling or stock discrepancies, consuming hours of administrative time.
solution: By integrating the Make connector within Claude, managers can trigger automated inventory synchronization scenarios. Claude acts as the orchestration layer, using the Make API to query data stores, compare records, and execute update scenarios when discrepancies are detected, effectively closing the loop between inventory logs and sales channels.
steps: Authenticate the Make connector within the Claude interface using your organization API credentials.
Use the data-stores_list tool to identify the specific inventory data store containing current stock levels.
Configure a Claude prompt to analyze the data-store-records and identify items where stock levels fall below a defined threshold.
Invoke the scenarios_run tool to trigger a pre-built Make scenario that updates the storefront inventory database.
Verify the update by calling data-store-records_get to confirm the new stock values are reflected.
outcome: A streamlined, error-resistant inventory management process where stock adjustments are handled through natural language commands rather than manual spreadsheet updates.
limitation: The connector relies on the existing structure of Make scenarios; if a scenario fails due to an external API timeout in the downstream service, Claude will report the failure but cannot automatically debug the external service's connectivity issues. Users must check the Make scenario execution logs directly in the Make dashboard to diagnose root causes.
